items.ig_caption:
99% less likely to be hacked. One setting. 🔑

Cybersecurity from Zero · Part 2: why your password isn't enough.

→ Myth: a strong password keeps you safe
→ Reality: a password is one credential. If it leaks, gets guessed or gets phished, whoever has it is you
→ MFA (multi-factor authentication) asks for two or more credentials at login, per CISA
→ CISA says using MFA makes you 99% less likely to be hacked

Do it today: turn on MFA for your email first (it resets everything else), then banking and social accounts.

Send this to the friend who reuses one password 👇

Source: CISA, Multifactor Authentication

#MFA #CyberSecurityForBeginners #LearnCyberSecurity #PasswordSecurity #CyberSecurity #InfoSec

segments.show: Cybersecurity from Zero · Part 3: spot a phishing message.

segments.say: CISA says bad spelling is no longer a reliable sign. A I writes clean scams.
segments.show: Look instead for: urgency, requests for personal or financial info, shortened links, lookalike addresses like amazan.com.

segments.say: Don't click. Report it, delete it, and contact the company through its official site.
segments.show: Never use the link or phone number in the message to check it.

items.ig_caption:
Perfect grammar. Still phishing. 🎣

Cybersecurity from Zero · Part 3: spot a phishing message.

→ CISA says poor grammar and spelling are no longer reliable signs, because AI writes polished messages
→ Watch for urgent or emotional pressure, especially threats of bad things if you don't act now
→ Watch for requests for personal or financial information
→ Watch for shortened links and lookalike addresses, like amazan.com

What to do: don't click or reply. Report it, delete it, and check with the company through its official website, never the link or number in the message.
